tagline: Colored sandstone and abandoned borax mines along a desert byway
intro: Bitter Springs Back Country Byway passes the Muddy Mountains, colored sandstone and traces of vanished rivers. The Bureau of Land Management lists it as a Type II Back Country Byway and highlights its rock formations and abandoned borax mines. The agency allows two to four hours for the 28-mile drive.
BLM identifies abandoned borax mines along the road, alongside evidence of rivers that have long since dried up.

From Valley of Fire Highway, the unimproved Bitter Spring Trail crosses the northwest of the Muddy Mountains into the northern part of Bitter Spring Valley. It continues through the valley and Bitter Spring Wash toward Echo Bay, on the Overton Arm of Lake Mead.

moments.title: Muddy Mountains
moments.text: The Muddy Mountains surround the northern section of Bitter Spring Valley. Coming from Valley of Fire Highway, the unimproved route crosses the northwest of the range before entering the valley. Within the mountains, Congress established the 48,154-acre Muddy Mountains Wilderness in 2002. BLM and the National Park Service manage that wilderness, where elevations range from 1,700 to 5,400 feet.

moments.title: Bitter Spring Valley
moments.text: Bitter Ridge divides Bitter Spring Valley into two sections. Its four-mile arc separates the longer southern section from a northern basin bordered by the Muddy Mountains to the west, northwest and north. Water from the northern section drains southeast into two washes; the southern washes combine and flow toward Echo Bay. Muddy Peak, at 5,363 feet, borders the valley directly to the west, adjacent to Bitter Ridge but not connected to it.

moments.title: Echo Bay and Bitter Spring Wash
moments.text: At Echo Bay, Bitter Spring Wash reaches the Overton Arm of Lake Mead. The valley lies on the lake’s western edge, between bordering mountain ranges. North Shore Road provides the major southern approach to Echo Bay and the eastern valley, crossing the northeastern sections of the Black Mountains. The wash, valley and mountain crossing described here belong to the unimproved route that connects Echo Bay with Valley of Fire Highway.

practical: Muddy Mountains: High-clearance vehicles are required; four-wheel drive is recommended. (checked 2026-10-11)
